messages.subject: Bifactor Model Specifying Orthogonal Factors
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'd like to estimate the SNP effects of my latent factor in a bifactor model. Is there a way to estimate SNP effects and specify orthogonality between factors?

When I run my bifactor model with the lines specifying that I want orthogonal factors (i.e., the "~~ 0*" lines), I get the following error:

[1] "Please note that an update was made to userGWAS on 11/21/19 so that it combines addSNPs and userGWAS." [1] "Starting GWAS Estimation" error calling combine function: <simpleError in rbind(deparse.level, ...): numbers of columns of arguments do not match> Error in order(results$i) : argument 1 is not a vector

Here is my code. It works fine when I remove all the orthogonality constraints.

gwasmodel <- 'Internalizing =~ Neff_Meta_Dep + Neff_Meta_OCD + Neff_Meta_PTSD + Neff_Meta_SH + Neff_Meta_Eat_Rev + Neff_Meta_ANX
Thought_Disorder =~ a*SCZ_colUK+ a*Neff_Meta_BPD
Externalizing =~ b*Other.Substance.Hazard.Dependence_ukb + b*Neff_Meta_AUD

P =~ Neff_Meta_Dep + Neff_Meta_PTSD + Neff_Meta_OCD + Neff_Meta_SH + Neff_Meta_Eat_Rev + Neff_Meta_ANX + SCZ_colUK+ Neff_Meta_BPD + Other.Substance.Hazard.Dependence_ukb + Neff_Meta_AUD

P ~~ 0*Thought_Disorder
P ~~ 0*Internalizing
P ~~ 0*Externalizing

Internalizing ~~ 0*Thought_Disorder
Externalizing ~~ 0*Internalizing
Thought_Disorder ~~ 0*Externalizing
'
gwas <- userGWAS(covstruc = LDSCoutput,
                      SNPs = d1,
                      estimation = "DWLS",
                      model = gwasmodel,
                      sub=c("P~SNP"),
                      GC = "standard")
Thanks!

Camille

messages.subject: Running userGWAS results in R being killed after all free memory has been consumed
messages.subject_clean: Running userGWAS results in R being killed after all free memory has been consumed
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to run GWAS-by-subtraction in GenomicSEM and I am having out-of-memory issues. I am following the steps and models that are described in this tutorial: https://rpubs.com/MichelNivard/565885. The input is having more than 10 million SNPs. When running the analysis for top 1 million, the process completed successfully.
When running with 10M SNPs the userGWAS function consumes all the free memory (which is around 26GB) and then R gets killed. I am running this function using parallel=TRUE on a Linux machine with 8 cores and 16 threads. I have set the correct environment variables before starting R (export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1).
I have also tried to reduce the amount of cores allocated for the function and this results in less memory being used initially but I am not sure if it actually postpones the process being killed or it can really help in avoiding the out-of-memory issues.

Do you have any ideas how to solve this issue, can decreasing the amount of cores actually result in a smaller memory usage or it will only result in memory being used up more slowly but initially still in the same amount? Are there any other tips or tricks to try to get this function running?

Thank you for your help!
Kätlin

messages.subject: Re: Running userGWAS results in R being killed after all free memory has been consumed
messages.subject_clean: Running userGWAS results in R being killed after all free memory has been consumed
messages.body_plain:
Hi  Kätlin,

Lowering the number of cores in userGWAS will definitely save quite a bit of memory (as will setting the correct exports btw), as each core spawns a new R process with its own memory overhead, input data, etc. I tested this once albeit on a much smaller dataset and on windows (See v0.0.5 in PATCHNOTES.md on github), and memory usage of 12 cores was roughly 4x that of 1 core, though I should point out I expect the scaling to be less severe on Windows. So all in all, yes, lowering the cores will lower memory usage.

However, lowering these significantly will lead to much slower runtimes than your machine is capable of which would be unfortunate, and I can't guarantee that it will be sufficient to solve all memory problems. What I would recommend you do is splitting your input data and running those separately, as follows:
Rscript1: Runs everything up to your call to userGWAS, then saves a number of files with what will be the input of SNPs split into, let's say 5 parts with ~2M SNPs each. This should also save covstruc and everything else you provide as input to userGWAS.
Rscript2: Runs userGWAS for a specific part (for how to provide arguments to an R script see https://www.r-bloggers.com/2015/09/passing-arguments-to-an-r-script-from-command-lines/) with input generated in Rscript1, saves the result of that part
Rscript3: Merges all X (5 in my example) parts of Rscript2, how to do this will depend on the model and sub argument, but likely boils down to rbinding the individual elements of the resulting list. Everything else you want to do after userGWAS also goes here.

This will of course still be slower than doing it all in 1 go, but I expect the runtime difference to be much smaller compared to a run with cores=4 instead of cores=15.
All that being said,  this is more work than just lowering cores... So if runtime is not an issue at all, lowering the cores argument would be the easiest way.

Let me know if that helps!

Best,
Matthijs

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Mattijs for your quick response.

Can you provide some information about your systems hardware and OS.

-> I was working on calculation servers in our institute and the OS of all servers are the same (Debian Testing), but the CPUs are totally different among them.

Also, are you running the latest version of GSEM? And could add the code you are running (or at least the commonfactorGWAS and userGWAS calls)?

-> Yes, running with the latest version and the following codes with masking phenotypes. If you need, I could send you privately whole codes and log files for each phenotype.

*As a piece of additional information, these GWAS summary stats are derived from all continuous traits.

Best,
Ryo

# Read packages
library(devtools); require(GenomicSEM)

## munge the summary statistics files##
## note that we include the argument names (e.g., files, hm3) for
## completeness in the code below, but that this is not necessary to run the code.
munge(files = c("A_withRS.txt",
                "B_withRS.txt",
                "C_withRS.txt",
                "D_withRS.txt"),
      hm3 = "w_hm3.snplist",
      trait.names = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
      info.filter = 0.7, maf.filter = 0.01)

# Run multivariable LDSC
traits <- c("A.sumstats.gz", "B.sumstats.gz", "C.sumstats.gz", "D.sumstats.gz")
sample.prev <- c(rep(NA, 4))
population.prev <- c(rep(NA, 4))
ld <- "eur_w_ld_chr/"
wld <- "eur_w_ld_chr/"
trait.names <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")
LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits = traits, sample.prev = sample.prev, population.prev = population.prev, ld = ld, wld = wld, trait.names = trait.names)

# Prepare the summary statistics for GWAS
files <- c("A_withRS.txt",
           "B_withRS.txt",
           "C_withRS.txt",
           "D_withRS.txt")
ref <- "reference.1000G.maf.0.005.txt"
trait.names <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")
se.logit <- c(F, F, F, F)
info.filter <- 0.7
maf.filter <- 0.01

sumstats <- sumstats(files = files, ref = ref, trait.names = trait.names,
                     se.logit = se.logit, OLS = c(T, T, T, T), linprob = NULL, N = NULL, beta = NULL, info.filter = info.filter, maf.filter = maf.filter,
                     keep.indel = FALSE, parallel = TRUE, cores = 24)

# Define use model for Heywood case
model <- "F1 =~ A + B + C + D
          F1 ~~ 1*F1
          F1 ~ SNP"

# Run the commonfactor GWAS using userGWAS function
factor <- userGWAS(covstruc = LDSCoutput, SNPs = sumstats, estimation = "DWLS", model = model, parallel = TRUE, cores = 24)
write.csv(factor, "result.csv", row.names = F)

messages.subject: SNP order causing an error
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am running a common factor GWAS and found a peculiar issue/bug. Essentially when I run a set of SNPs in a certain order while parallel=True, it would cause the error:

error calling combine function: <simpleError in match.names(clabs, names(xi)): names do not match previous names>.

Let's say that there are SNP1 and SNP2. When the GWAS is run with order [SNP1,SNP2], the above error is shown. When the order is reversed, the GWAS runs fine with no lavaan warnings or errors in the results. SNP2 runs fine on its own, but when SNP1 is run on its own, it generates a lavaan error:

lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

When parallel=F, original order produces the optimizer error but the reversed order again runs without any lavaan warnings.

Below is the sample code I ran. The example was run with core=1, but this issue was originally found with core=30. Rest of the GWAS ran successfully without issues.

# reinstall to ensure that we are running the latest GSEM
devtools::install_github("GenomicSEM/GenomicSEM", force=TRUE)
library(GenomicSEM)

LDSC_PATH <- "bugtest/LDSC.RDS"
SUMSTAT_PATH <- "bugtest/bugtest.Sumstats.RDS"
# set input variables
ldsc_res <- readRDS(LDSC_PATH)
aligned_sumstats <- readRDS(SUMSTAT_PATH)

# 1. test with all in initial order
test_defaultorder <- commonfactorGWAS(
covstruc = ldsc_res,
SNPs = aligned_sumstats[1:2,],
cores=1
)
# this causes error calling combine function
# 2. flip the sumstat order
row1 <- aligned_sumstats[1,]
row2 <- aligned_sumstats[2,]
aligned_sumstats_flipped <- rbind(row2, row1)

test_flipped <- commonfactorGWAS(
covstruc = ldsc_res,
SNPs = aligned_sumstats_flipped,
cores=1
)
# this runs successfully (0.927 seconds) with legible results

# 3. just SNP1
test_snp1 <- commonfactorGWAS(
covstruc = ldsc_res,
SNPs = row1,
cores=1
)
# runs with significantly higher runtime (12 seconds) and produces lavaan error

# 4. just SNP2
test_snp2 <- commonfactorGWAS(
covstruc = ldsc_res,
SNPs = row2,
cores=1
)
# runs successfully (0.589 seconds) with legible results that is identical to flipped test above

# 5. parallel flag set to FALSE
test_defaultorder_noparallel <- commonfactorGWAS(
covstruc = ldsc_res,
SNPs = aligned_sumstats[1:2,],
parallel=F
)
# runs with significantly higher runtime (11 seconds) and produces lavaan error
test_flipped_multicore <- commonfactorGWAS(
covstruc = ldsc_res,
SNPs = aligned_sumstats_flipped,
parallel=F
)
# runs successfully (0.89 seconds) with no lavaan errors

Wanted to make sure this was a bug rather an a potential issue with my LDSC results or summary statistics. I can provide the LDSC results, the summary statistics, and Jupyter Notebook of the above code via email.

Regards,

Jeff

Op maandag 16 mei 2022 om 23:09:14 UTC+2 schreef kim...@nih.gov:

> Hi everyone,
>
> I am running a common factor GWAS and found a peculiar issue/bug. Essentially when I run a set of SNPs in a certain order while parallel=True, it would cause the error:
>
> error calling combine function: <simpleError in match.names(clabs, names(xi)): names do not match previous names>.
>
> Let's say that there are SNP1 and SNP2. When the GWAS is run with order [SNP1,SNP2], the above error is shown. When the order is reversed, the GWAS runs fine with no lavaan warnings or errors in the results. SNP2 runs fine on its own, but when SNP1 is run on its own, it generates a lavaan error:
>
> lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!
>
> When parallel=F, original order produces the optimizer error but the reversed order again runs without any lavaan warnings.
>
> Below is the sample code I ran. The example was run with core=1, but this issue was originally found with core=30. Rest of the GWAS ran successfully without issues.
>
> # reinstall to ensure that we are running the latest GSEM
> devtools::install_github("GenomicSEM/GenomicSEM", force=TRUE)
> library(GenomicSEM)
>
> LDSC_PATH <- "bugtest/LDSC.RDS"
> SUMSTAT_PATH <- "bugtest/bugtest.Sumstats.RDS"
> # set input variables
> ldsc_res <- readRDS(LDSC_PATH)
> aligned_sumstats <- readRDS(SUMSTAT_PATH)
>
> # 1. test with all in initial order
> test_defaultorder <- commonfactorGWAS(
> covstruc = ldsc_res,
> SNPs = aligned_sumstats[1:2,],
> cores=1
> )
> # this causes error calling combine function
> # 2. flip the sumstat order
> row1 <- aligned_sumstats[1,]
> row2 <- aligned_sumstats[2,]
> aligned_sumstats_flipped <- rbind(row2, row1)
>
> test_flipped <- commonfactorGWAS(
> covstruc = ldsc_res,
> SNPs = aligned_sumstats_flipped,
> cores=1
> )
> # this runs successfully (0.927 seconds) with legible results
>
> # 3. just SNP1
> test_snp1 <- commonfactorGWAS(
> covstruc = ldsc_res,
> SNPs = row1,
> cores=1
> )
> # runs with significantly higher runtime (12 seconds) and produces lavaan error
>
> # 4. just SNP2
> test_snp2 <- commonfactorGWAS(
> covstruc = ldsc_res,
> SNPs = row2,
> cores=1
> )
> # runs successfully (0.589 seconds) with legible results that is identical to flipped test above
>
> # 5. parallel flag set to FALSE
> test_defaultorder_noparallel <- commonfactorGWAS(
> covstruc = ldsc_res,
> SNPs = aligned_sumstats[1:2,],
> parallel=F
> )
> # runs with significantly higher runtime (11 seconds) and produces lavaan error
> test_flipped_multicore <- commonfactorGWAS(
> covstruc = ldsc_res,
> SNPs = aligned_sumstats_flipped,
> parallel=F
> )
> # runs successfully (0.89 seconds) with no lavaan errors
>
> Wanted to make sure this was a bug rather an a potential issue with my LDSC results or summary statistics. I can provide the LDSC results, the summary statistics, and Jupyter Notebook of the above code via email.
>
> Regards,
>
> Jeff

messages.subject: Prerequisite for running commonfactorGWAS
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

We are using Genomic SEM's commonfactorGWAS to generate summary statistics with 7 traits (Fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, TRG, HDL, Waist circumference, SBP, DBP). Our aim is to generate a PRS score for Metabolic syndrome.
Some GWAS summary statistics are presented in reference to the allele on the forward strand (TRG, HDL, SBP, DBP) while others are in the reverse strand (HOMA-IR, FG, WC). My questions are the following:

1- Should the summary statistics reported on the reverse strands be flipped to the forward strand before munging?

2- Additionally, some of our traits are from the same cohort study. Is it okay to munge GWAS summary statistics if more than 1 trait are from the same study population

3- Should the effect allele be arranged such that the allele shows increased risk?

Thanks in advance.

Best regards,
Rajini

messages.subject: Re: User Specified Model GWAS Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anthony,
It doesn't look like you have an identification constraint for F2 so your model probably isn't identified. Try removing the NA before the loading of Phen4 so that you have unit loading identification for F2.
Btw, I would recommend trying the model out without SNPs to make sure it converges before adding in SNPs.
Elliot

messages.subject: Calculating sample size for factors
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I made a factor model consisting of four traits and did userGWAS. I calculated the sample size for factors with the code from wiki to calculate the genome-wide polygenic risk score (GPS) for V1 as the output of userGWAS, and it seems that the number was too large.

My questions are the following:

1. Is the factor model consisting of the traits (V1 to V3: binary traits, V4: quantitative trait) that I set appropriate?

LDSCouput:

Model:

Model <- "F1=~NA*V1+V2+V3+V4

F1~~1*F1”

Modelfit:

2. When I obtained the effective sample size with the above code on the wiki, 792546.3 came out. Why is there such a large number of effective sample sizes?

Using software called LDpred2, the UK Biobank sample is used to calculate the polygenic risk score for V1. It is calculated with the output from Genomic SEM, and due to the influence of neff, heritability is too small compared to the single V1 summary’s heritability (0.17546).

Each effective sample size:

V1 : 41,524

V2 : 226,894

V3 : 44,204

V4 : 371,949

Best wishes,

Shinyoung
